common.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.

overview.title: Overview
overview.text: What the agents are doing with your databases, and how well protected they are.
overview.activityText: Every call an agent made to pgharbor, by result.
overview.quietText: No agent called pgharbor in the period chosen. Pick a longer one, or come back after a session.
overview.toolsText: Which tools the agents reach for. Select one to see its calls.
overview.rulesText: Which safety rule stopped a call. Many refusals by one rule usually mean the agent needs a hint, not that the rule is wrong.
overview.hoursText: When pgharbor is used, in your local time.
overview.noRefusals: Nothing was refused in this period.
overview.noSessions: No client is connected right now.
posture.title: Security posture
posture.text: The hardening checklist, applied to your configuration.
posture.invalid: The configuration is not valid, so it cannot be assessed.
posture.forConnection: What to review in this connection
posture.all-good: Nothing in the configuration needs attention
posture.all-good.help: Production is read-only and asks for approval, functions are inspected, the log is on.
posture.secret-in-file: A credential is written in the file ({keys})
posture.secret-in-file.help: Prefer the name of an environment variable (password_env, dsn_env) or a password file: the configuration file is then safe to read and to back up.
posture.file-readable-by-others: The file holds a credential and other users of this computer can read it (mode {mode})
posture.file-readable-by-others.help: Run chmod 600 on the file. The panel writes it that way on every save.
posture.file-writable-by-others: Other users of this computer can change the file (mode {mode})
posture.file-writable-by-others.help: Whoever writes this file decides what the agents can do. Run chmod 600 on it.
posture.audit-is-off.help: Nothing an agent does is being recorded, and this panel cannot show sessions. Turn it on in Audit.
posture.audit-without-sql: The log does not record statements
posture.audit-without-sql.help: You can see that a tool ran, but not what it ran.
posture.audit-logs-values: The log records the values bound to statements
posture.audit-logs-values.help: Useful to reproduce a call; remember that those values may be personal data and that the log is a file on disk.
posture.production-writes.help: Each write still asks for your confirmation, but read-only is the setting that cannot go wrong.
posture.production-without-approval: Production can be used without your approval
posture.production-without-approval.help: Set approval to ask each session, so that an agent can never reach production as a fallback.
posture.production-without-cost-ceiling: Production has no ceiling for the cost of a query
Set max_plan_cost to refuse a query that the planner estimates as too heavy before it runs.
posture.production-fallback-conversation: Without a dialog, production trusts the conversation
In clients that cannot show a dialog, the agent's statement that you asked for production is accepted. Set the fallback to refuse if you never use such clients.
posture.production-explain-analyze: EXPLAIN ANALYZE is allowed in production
posture.production-explain-analyze.help: It really executes the query to time it, with its full cost.
posture.functions-permissive.help: With the permissive policy any function runs, except the always-refused list. Use standard or strict.
posture.secret-catalogs-exposed: The catalogs with password hashes are readable
posture.secret-catalogs-exposed.help: pg_authid, pg_shadow and the like hold credentials of the server. Keep them denied.
posture.writes-without-dialog: Writes do not ask you in a dialog (confirmation: {mode})
posture.writes-without-dialog.help: A dialog is answered by you, not by the model. The other modes are conventions.
posture.redaction-off.help: Columns named password, token, secret and similar normally come back as [redacted].
posture.functions-vouched: {count} function is trusted without inspection|{count} functions are trusted without inspection
posture.functions-vouched.help: Listing a function in allow_functions vouches for everything it does. Keep the list to functions you have read.
posture.no-tls-required: The connection does not require encryption (sslmode: {sslmode})
posture.no-tls-required.help: For a server on another machine, set the parameter sslmode to require or, better, verify-full.
risk.no-baseline: There was no valid configuration to compare with
risk.no-baseline.help: The whole file counts as new. Read it as you would read a configuration someone handed you.
risk.production-without-approval: Production will be usable without your approval
risk.functions-permissive: Functions will not be inspected on this connection
risk.secret-catalogs-exposed: The catalogs with password hashes become readable
risk.access-raised.help: The agent will be able to change this database, not only read it.
risk.approval-removed: Using this connection will no longer need your approval
risk.environment-demoted: The environment goes from {before} to {after}: it stops counting as production
risk.approval-fallback-weakened: Without a dialog, the agent's word will be accepted as your approval
risk.write-confirmation-weakened: Confirmation of writes goes from {before} to {after}
risk.function-policy-weakened: The function policy goes from {before} to {after}
risk.functions-allowed.help: Listing a function vouches for everything it does, including the tables it reads.
risk.explain-analyze-allowed: EXPLAIN ANALYZE will really execute queries
risk.export-allowed: Results can be exported to files
risk.limit-raised: The limit {key} goes up, from {before} to {after}
risk.cost-ceiling-raised: The ceiling for the cost of a query goes from {before} to {after}
risk.role-changed: The role assumed in each transaction changes, from {before} to {after}
risk.target-changed: This connection will point somewhere else ({keys})
risk.ssl-weakened: Encryption of the connection is weakened: sslmode from {before} to {after}
risk.protection-removed: The table {table} is no longer protected
risk.index-filter-dropped: {table} can be read without an index filter
risk.protected-rows-raised: More rows of {table} per query: from {before} to {after}
risk.audit-disabled: The audit log is turned off
risk.audit-disabled.help: Nothing the agents do will be recorded, and the list of sessions stops.
risk.audit-params-on: The log starts recording the values bound to statements
risk.audit-params-on.help: Those values may be personal data, and the log is a file on disk.
risk.tool-group-enabled: The tool group {group} is offered again
risk.custom-tool-added.help: A custom tool is a statement you vouch for. Read it once more before saving.
risk.custom-tool-sql-changed: The statement of the custom tool {tool} changes
risk.custom-tool-scope-widened: The custom tool {tool} becomes available on more connections
risk.custom-tool-rows-raised: The custom tool {tool} may return more rows
risk.default-is-production: The default connection becomes a production one
risk.connection-added.help: The agents gain a new database to reach. Check where it points and with which role.
risk.params-changed: Connection parameters that decide what is trusted change: {keys}
risk.export-dir-changed: The folder exports are written to changes
risk.export-dir-changed.help: The export tool writes files there. Do not point it at a folder whose files matter.
risk.import-dir-changed: The folder the CSV import reads from changes
risk.import-dir-changed.help: The agent can load any file of that folder into a table. Do not point it at a folder with private files.
risk.protection-rearranged: The rules for protected tables were rearranged
risk.protection-rearranged.help: The first rule that matches a table is the one in force. A rule placed before another can take its place: check each protected table.
risk.audit-path-changed: The audit log moves to another file
risk.audit-path-changed.help: What the agents do stops being written where you look for it today.
risk.role-changed.help: Every transaction runs as this role. Make sure it is not a stronger one.
risk.target-changed.help: The same name will lead to another server, database or user. Approvals and rules follow the name, not the place.
save.doneBackup: Saved. The previous version was kept as {name}.
save.invalid: This would not be a valid configuration
save.invalidHelp: pgharbor's own validator refused it, so nothing was written. Fix the points below and try again.
save.weakensHelp: Each point below lets an agent do more than it can today. Read them before going on.
save.safe: This change does not reduce the protection
save.safeHelp: Nothing in it lets an agent do more than it can today.
save.notes: {n} thing to know|{n} things to know
save.diffHelp: Lines starting with + are added, lines starting with - are removed. Credentials are masked.
save.when: At the start of the next session. A client that is already connected keeps the rules it started with until it reconnects.
save.whenActive: At the start of the next session. {n} client connected now keeps its current rules until it reconnects.|At the start of the next session. {n} clients connected now keep their current rules until they reconnect.
save.acknowledge: I have read the points above and want to save anyway
unsaved.title: Leave without saving?
unsaved.text: The changes you made on this screen have not been saved and will be lost.
error.network: The panel is not answering. It may have been stopped.
error.conflict: The configuration file changed on disk since this screen read it. Reload and try again.
error.read-only: The panel was started in read-only mode.
error.invalid: The configuration would not be valid.
error.toml: The file is not valid TOML, so it cannot be edited here. Fix it in a text editor or restore an earlier version.
error.no-file: There is no configuration file yet. Create it on the File screen.
error.acknowledge: This change reduces the protection and needs your confirmation.
error.io: The file could not be read or written.
error.internal: The panel hit an internal error. See the terminal where it runs.
banner.invalid: The configuration file is not valid
banner.invalidText: Sessions that start now cannot use it. See what is wrong and fix it, or restore an earlier version.
banner.environment: The connection comes from environment variables
banner.missing: The configuration file was not found
banner.noFileText: Create a configuration file to manage connections and rules here.
readonly.title: Nothing can be changed here
readonly.text: The panel was started with --read-only. Start it without that option to edit.
readonly.noFile: There is no valid configuration file to edit. See the File screen.
lock.title: Open the panel with its key
lock.text: This panel only opens with the address printed in the terminal by the command below. The address carries a key that is new on every start.
lock.label: Address or key
lock.help: Paste the whole address, or only the key. It stays in this browser tab and is sent only to the panel on this computer.
lock.invalid: That does not look like the address printed by pgharbor ui.
lock.expired: The key is no longer valid. The panel was probably restarted: use the new address.
panel.title: Panel
panel.text: This panel: how it looks, what this run can do and how it is protected.
panel.themeHelp: System follows the light or dark setting of your computer.
panel.runText: The panel exists only while the command that started it is running.
panel.idleValue: after {n} minute without use|after {n} minutes without use
panel.stopText: This page stops working until pgharbor ui is started again. The agents are not affected: the MCP servers keep running.
panel.stoppedText: It was stopped, or it stopped by itself after a while without use. Start it again in a terminal and open the new address:
panel.docsNote: These links open the project's pages on GitHub in a new tab. Nothing about your installation is sent.
guard.title: How this panel is protected
guard.text: It can change which databases an agent reaches, so it is built to be hard to reach.
guard.local.title: Only on this computer
guard.local.text: It listens on 127.0.0.1 and nowhere else. No other machine on the network can reach it.
guard.key.title: A key that is new on every start
guard.key.text: The address in the terminal carries a random key. Without it the panel answers nothing. The key is kept only in this browser tab, never in a cookie.
guard.sites.title: Other websites cannot use it
guard.sites.text: A page open in your browser cannot make requests here: the panel checks where each request comes from and which address it was sent to.
guard.review.title: Nothing is saved without a review
guard.review.text: Every change is judged by pgharbor's own validator, shown to you as a difference, and flagged when it reduces the protection.
guard.backup.title: Every change can be undone
guard.backup.text: The previous version of the file is kept on every save, and each save is written to the audit log.
guard.limit.title: What it does not protect against
guard.limit.text: A program running as you on this computer can edit the configuration file directly, with or without this panel. The boundary that holds is the database role the agent connects with.
pause.title: Emergency pause
pause.text: Stop the agents' access to the databases right now, without closing anything.
pause.cardText: The one switch that acts immediately.
pause.how: Every running pgharbor checks the pause before each access to a database, so it takes effect at once, in every session. It can only take access away, and it stays until you end it here.
pause.reasonPlaceholder: Optional, for example: investigating an incident
pause.lifted: The pause was ended. Access is back to the rules of the configuration.
pause.activeText: Agents are being refused until you end the pause.
pause.reach: It reaches the sessions listed under Sessions: {n} active now. A server started with another state directory is not reached.|It reaches the sessions listed under Sessions: {n} active now. A server started with another state directory is not reached.
sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.text: Who is using pgharbor: each client session, what it did and what it was allowed.
sessions.noneText: A session appears here when an MCP client (Claude Code, for example) starts pgharbor.
sessions.notRecordingText: The audit log is off, and the session files follow it. Turn the log on in Audit to see who is connected.
sessions.outdatedTitle: This session is using an older configuration
sessions.outdatedText: The file changed after the session started. It keeps the rules it started with until the client reconnects (in Claude Code: /mcp, then reconnect pgharbor).
sessions.someOutdated: {n} session is using an older configuration|{n} sessions are using an older configuration
sessions.how: Each client session starts its own pgharbor process. Each process keeps a small file while it runs, and marks its lines in the audit log with the same identifier. The name of the client is what the client said about itself.
connections.title: Connections
connections.text: The databases the agents can reach, and the rules of each one.
connections.newText: Start with where to connect. Everything you leave untouched keeps the safe default.
connections.defaultHelp: Used when a tool is called without naming a connection. With none, the agent must always name one.
connections.approvalNeeded: Needs your approval in each session
connections.emptyText: Add the first database the agents may reach.
connections.noFile: Create the configuration file first, on the File screen.
connections.gone: This connection does not exist any more
connections.nameHelp: What the agent passes as connection: lowercase letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 characters.
connections.nameInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits, - and _ (starting with a letter or a digit, up to 32 characters).
connections.nameTaken: There is already a connection with this name.
connections.renameText: What refers to it (the default connection, custom tools) follows the new name. Sessions that are running keep the old name until they reconnect.
connections.duplicateText: A copy with the same rules. Credentials written in the file are not copied: define them again in the copy.
connections.deleteText: The connection {name} will be removed from the configuration. Sessions that are running keep it until they reconnect.
connections.saveFirst: Save or discard the changes on this screen first.
connections.inUse: This connection is still in use
connections.inUseDefault: It is the default connection. Choose another default first.
connections.inUseTool: The custom tool {tool} is limited to it. Change that tool first.
test.title: Test of {name}
test.productionText: This opens a connection to {name} from this panel, to check that it works. Nothing is read or changed.
test.superuserText: pgharbor blocks the dangerous functions by name, which is one layer only. A dedicated role with just the privileges the agent needs is much safer.
test.environmentHint: The test runs in the panel's own process. If the user or the password come from environment variables, they must be set in the terminal that started the panel, which is not necessarily where the MCP client sets them.
defaults.title: Defaults
defaults.text: Rules and limits that every connection gets unless it sets its own.
defaults.how: A value set here applies to every connection that does not set that key itself ({n} connection configured). A key left alone here uses pgharbor's own default.|A value set here applies to every connection that does not set that key itself ({n} connections configured). A key left alone here uses pgharbor's own default.
group.identity.text: How this connection is presented to the agent and to you.
group.where.text: The server, and where the credentials come from. Credentials are best kept out of this file.
group.access.text: What the agent may do here, and what needs you.
group.functions.text: A read-only transaction does not stop a function from writing. This decides which functions may be called.
group.data.text: Tables and columns the agent must not read, and what leaves the database.
group.limits.text: Bounds on time and size, so that no query can flood the server or the conversation.
group.pool.text: How connections to the server are opened and kept.
field.env.set: The variable {name} is set where this panel runs.
field.env.unset: The variable {name} is not set where this panel runs. It may still be set where the MCP client starts pgharbor.
field.environment.isProduction: This name marks the connection as production: it needs your approval in each session.
field.description.label: Description
field.description.help: A line the agent sees in the list of connections. Say what the database is for.
field.environment.label: Environment
field.environment.help: A free label. The names production, prod, live and producao make the connection require approval.
field.host.label: Host
field.host.help: Name or address of the PostgreSQL server.
field.port.label: Port
field.dbname.label: Database
field.dbname.help: Name of the database on that server.
field.user.label: User
field.user.help: The role to connect as, written here. Use this or the variable below, not both.
field.user_env.label: User, from a variable
field.user_env.help: Name of the environment variable that holds the user name.
field.password_env.label: Password, from a variable
field.password_env.help: Name of the environment variable that holds the password. The recommended way: the password never touches this file.
field.password_file.label: Password, from a file
field.password_file.help: Path of a file whose content is the password.
field.password.label: Password, written in the file
field.password.help: Avoid it: prefer a variable or a password file. The panel never shows a password that is already here.
field.dsn_env.label: Connection string, from a variable
field.dsn_env.help: Name of the variable holding a whole connection string or URI, instead of host, port and database.
field.dsn.label: Connection string, written in the file
field.dsn.help: A whole connection string or URI. It may carry a password, so the panel never shows it.
field.role.label: Act as role
field.role.help: Runs SET ROLE in every transaction: connect as one user and act as a weaker one.
field.params.label: Connection parameters
field.params.help: Other libpq parameters, such as sslmode, sslrootcert or keepalives.
field.access.label: Access mode
field.access.help: Read-only: queries only. Read and write: also INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE and CALL. Administration: also DDL and maintenance.
field.access.warn.read-write: The agent will be able to change rows here. Each write still asks for your confirmation.
field.access.warn.admin: The agent will be able to change the structure of this database and run maintenance.
field.approval.label: Approval to use
field.approval.help: Whether you must approve this connection once in each session, in a dialog. By environment: asked for production only.
field.approval.warn.never: This connection will be usable without asking you, even if it is production.
field.approval_ttl.label: How long an approval lasts
field.approval_ttl.help: After this time the agent must ask again. Zero keeps the approval for the whole session.
field.approval_fallback.label: When the client cannot show a dialog
field.approval_fallback.help: Refuse, or accept the agent's statement that you asked for this environment. The second is a convention, not a control.
field.write_confirmation.label: Confirmation of writes
field.write_confirmation.help: Dialog: you confirm every write in a dialog. Conversation: the agent's statement that you said yes is accepted. None: writes just run.
field.write_confirmation.warn.conversati: The agent's own statement that you agreed is accepted. A convention, not a control.
field.write_confirmation.warn.none: Writes run without asking anyone. For automation and test databases only.
field.function_policy.label: Function policy
field.function_policy.help: Strict: only the functions you list. Standard: functions that do not write, with their source inspected. Permissive: anything but the always-refused list.
field.function_policy.warn.permissive: Nothing is inspected. For disposable development databases only.
field.allow_functions.label: Functions to trust
field.allow_functions.help: Functions accepted although they write or cannot be read. Listing one vouches for everything it does.
field.deny_functions.label: Functions to deny
field.deny_functions.help: Functions that are never acceptable on this connection.
field.protect.label: Protected tables
field.protect.help: Extra rules for tables that are huge or hold sensitive columns: columns that cannot be read, a filter by index, fewer rows.
field.deny_relations.label: Tables to deny
field.deny_relations.help: Tables and views that free SQL may not read at all.
field.redact_columns.label: Columns to mask
field.redact_columns.help: Regular expressions. A result column whose name matches comes back as [redacted]. It guards against accidents; use protected tables for columns that matter.
field.expose_secret_catalogs.label: Allow the credential catalogs
field.expose_secret_catalogs.help: Lets free SQL read pg_authid, pg_shadow and the other catalogs that hold credentials.
field.expose_secret_catalogs.warn.true: The agent will be able to read password hashes and stored credentials of this server.
field.allow_explain_analyze.label: Allow EXPLAIN ANALYZE
field.allow_explain_analyze.help: Lets the plan tool really execute a query to time it.
field.allow_explain_analyze.warn.true: EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs the whole query, with its full cost.
field.allow_export.label: Allow export to files
field.allow_export.help: Lets the export tool write query results to files in the export folder.
field.export_dir.label: Export folder
field.export_dir.help: The only folder the export tool writes to.
field.import_dir.label: Import folder
field.import_dir.help: The only folder the CSV import tool reads from.
field.statement_timeout.label: Time limit per statement
field.statement_timeout.help: A statement that runs longer is cancelled by the server.
field.lock_timeout.label: Wait for a lock
field.lock_timeout.help: How long a statement waits for a lock before giving up.
field.idle_in_transaction_session_timeou: A safety net: a transaction left open and idle this long is ended by the server.
field.max_rows.label: Rows by default
field.max_rows.help: Rows returned when the agent does not ask for a number.
field.max_rows_limit.label: Most rows an agent can ask for
field.max_rows_limit.help: The ceiling for a single answer, whatever the agent asks.
field.max_cell_chars.label: Characters per value
field.max_cell_chars.help: A longer value is cut on the server, before it leaves the database.
field.max_result_chars.label: Characters per answer
field.max_result_chars.help: When the rows of an answer reach this size, the answer stops and says there is more.
field.max_sql_chars.label: Longest statement
field.max_sql_chars.help: A statement with more characters is refused.
field.max_plan_cost.label: Cost ceiling
field.max_plan_cost.help: Refuses a query whose estimated cost is higher, before it runs. In planner units; empty means no ceiling.
field.pool_size.label: Connections kept
field.pool_size.help: How many connections to the server are kept for this profile. Calls beyond that wait.
field.idle_close.label: Close when idle
field.idle_close.help: An unused connection is closed after this long. Zero closes after every call.
field.connect_timeout.label: Wait for the server
field.connect_timeout.help: How long to wait when opening a connection.
field.application_name.label: Application name
field.application_name.help: What the server shows for these connections, in pg_stat_activity for example.
field.table.label: Table
field.table.help: As schema.table. Patterns such as audit.* work.
field.deny_columns.label: Columns that cannot be read
field.deny_columns.help: They cannot be selected, filtered on or used in an expression.
field.require_index_filter.label: Require a filter by index
field.require_index_filter.help: Refuses any query that would read the table without an index condition.
field.protect_max_rows.label: Row limit for this table
field.note.label: Hint for the agent
field.note.help: Added to refusals: say how the table should be queried.
field.enabled.label: Record calls
field.enabled.help: One line per tool call in the audit log, and one small file per session. Without it this panel has little to show.
field.enabled.warn.false: Nothing will be recorded: no audit log and no list of sessions.
field.path.label: Log file
field.path.help: Where the log is written. Leave empty for the usual place.
field.log_sql.label: Record statements
field.log_sql.help: Writes the SQL text of each call, with credentials inside it masked.
field.log_params.label: Record bound values
field.log_params.help: Also writes the values bound to $1, $2... and the arguments of custom tools.
field.log_params.warn.true: Those values may be personal data, and the log is a file on disk.
field.tool_name.label: Name
field.tool_name.help: The tool appears to the agent as pgx_ followed by this name.
field.tool_description.label: Description
field.tool_description.help: What the agent reads to decide when to call it. Say what it returns and for which question.
field.sql.label: Statement
field.sql.help: One read-only statement. Write $1, $2... where a value goes.
field.tool_params.label: Parameters
field.tool_params.help: One for each placeholder, in order.
field.tool_connections.label: Where it is available
field.tool_connections.help: Leave everything unticked to offer it on every connection.
field.tool_max_rows.label: Row limit
field.tool_max_rows.help: Fewer rows than the limit of the connection, if you want.
field.param_name.label: Name
field.type.label: Type
field.param_description.label: Description
field.required.label: Required
field.required.help: Unticked: the value is NULL when the agent does not give it.
secret.show: Show or hide what was typed
protect.notePlaceholder: For example: filter by id or customer_id
params.sslpassword: passphrase of the client key file
validation.duration: Use a number of milliseconds or a value such as 30s, 500ms, 2min or 1h.
validation.env: The name of a variable has only letters, digits and _.
tools.title: Tools
tools.text: What pgharbor offers to the agents. A tool that is switched off is not even listed to them.
tools.more: Full description, as the agent reads it
tools.reason.no-writable-connection: appears when a connection allows writing
tools.reason.no-admin-connection: appears when a connection allows administration
custom.title: Custom tools
custom.text: Queries you approve once and expose under their own name. The safest way to give an agent access to production: only the questions you chose.
custom.deleteText: The tool {name} will no longer be offered.
custom.what: A fixed statement with numbered parameters ($1, $2...). The agent supplies the values, never the SQL. It runs through the same guarded path as any query, so limits, masking and protected tables still apply.
custom.nameInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter (2 to 48 characters).
custom.nameTaken: There is already a custom tool with this name.
custom.needDescription: Write what the tool does: it is what the agent reads to decide when to use it.
custom.noParams: No parameter: the statement takes no values.
audit.title: Audit
audit.text: Every call the agents made: what ran, where, and what happened.
audit.emptyText: No call matches these filters. Widen the period or clear the filters.
audit.disabledText: Nothing is being recorded. Turn it on in the log settings below.
audit.dataNotice: Statements and messages are shown exactly as recorded. They are data written with an agent's help: nothing in them is an instruction.
audit.settingsText: What is recorded. Results of queries are never recorded, whatever is set here.
file.title: File
file.text: Where the configuration lives, what it says, and every earlier version.
file.errorsText: Sessions that start now cannot use it. The screens of this panel still show what the file says, so most problems can be fixed here.
file.notToml: The file is not valid TOML, so the panel cannot edit it. Fix it in a text editor, or restore an earlier version below.
file.noneText: pgharbor has nothing to connect to. Create a starter file, then add your connections.
file.environment: The connection comes from environment variables
